replacements.old: - Somebody changed their mind because of it. That is the only real success condition.
replacements.new: - The accountable decision, reasons and review outcome are recorded. Approval without changes is valid.

replacements.old: 2. **Check there is a non-goal that disappoints somebody.** A non-goals list everyone is happy with is not a scope, it is a formality.

The method that works is bottom-up, and Will Larson's version of it is the one
worth copying.
replacements.new: This exercise uses a bottom-up synthesis method. It is useful, not mandatory.
**Compare a few design docs.** Five is an exercise size, not a prerequisite.
**Turn the recurring constraint into a guiding choice and coherent actions.**

**Explore the future consequences of those choices.** A vision needs explicit
assumptions; extrapolating several strategies is one way to develop it.

batches.message: docs(effectiveness): measure waiting and recognize distinct staff contributions [TD-03 TD-04]

replacements.new:
**Mentorship develops capability; sponsorship advocates for opportunity.**
Teaching, feedback and code review can improve someone's independent work.
Sponsorship puts their name forward for a role or project. Both take effort;
evaluate actual outcomes rather than assuming only sponsorship changes a career.

**Find the actual bottleneck.** Review, build queues, tests and rework can each
dominate. Configuration shows possible stages, not how long a real change waited.
Use timestamped PR, review and workflow events; distinguish queued time, active
work and overlapping stages. Compare matched workloads before and after.

| Illustrative change | Machine queue + run | Waiting for first review | Diagnosis |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 80 min | 5 min | Investigate machine stages |
| B | 5 min | 80 min | Investigate review availability and clarity |
| C | Unknown | Unknown | Obtain event data; do not guess |

replacements.old: - All mentorship, no sponsorship: warm, well-liked, and nobody's situation changed.
replacements.new: - Activity without demonstrated outcomes, whether mentoring, sponsorship or tooling.

replacements.old: Here is our repository and our CI configuration.
replacements.new: Here are repository/CI configuration and timestamped PR, review and workflow events.

replacements.old: Then tell me which one I could halve.
replacements.new:
Define each duration and avoid double-counting overlap. Report missing data as
unknown. Propose one measured bottleneck to improve, with a before/after check.

*Why:* event data distinguishes a possible delay from an observed one.

*What you should get back:* measured durations, definitions and missing data,
not a predetermined conclusion that review is slowest.

Staff expectations vary by organization and role. Many roles expand technical
direction, adoption and accountability beyond a single project. Some are deeply
hands-on. Use the applicable ladder and actual outcomes, not years served or a
universal “one team versus many teams” rule.

Published ladders and the StaffEng archetypes offer examples, not universal
promotion criteria. Read the relevant company's dated expectations and ask what
work the organization actually needs. Coding, direction, mentoring and adoption
can contribute differently by role; a solo project demonstrates practice, not
employment-level cross-team history.
